card: Bumps the minimum supported Xcode Command Line Tools version for native macOS builds from 16.2 to 26.3, updating documentation and macOS CI. This drops support for native builds on end-of-life macOS 14 (Sonoma) to ensure the native Apple Clang toolchain reaches an equivalent of LLVM 19. According to the author, raising this baseline is needed to enable C++20 class template argument deduction (CTAD) and prepare the project for C++23, without affecting depends-based release builds.

enables: Use of C++20 CTAD and upgrading the project baseline to C++23

evidence: Author notes in the description that macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 reached EOL with its final security update on August 6, 2026.
Author states in the description that upgrading CLT to 26.3 provides an LLVM-19 equivalent toolchain, which 'will allow to use C++20 CTAD and also allow switching the project to C++23.'
problem: Supporting older Xcode CLT versions restricts compiler capabilities on macOS, preventing the codebase from adopting newer C++ features. In addition, the underlying macOS 14 (Sonoma) operating system reached end-of-life in August 2026.
summary: Bump the minimum supported Xcode Command Line Tools version for native macOS builds from 16.2 to 26.3. The update modifies dependency documentation, release notes, and switches the CI runner to use Xcode 26.3.
